scope: Only the two named reference adaptations and this development manifest

upstream.author: Darrin Southern, CadenceUX
upstream.treatment: Retain/adapt CadenceUX explanatory prose with attribution. Independently replace all concrete examples, including secondary examples and application patterns; retain factual API signatures, parameter enumerations, version facts and caveats.
upstream.reason: Upstream CHANGELOG reports 143 primary examples copied from Claris documentation across the source collection. The number is not a count for these two files. Avoid redistributing those concrete examples without deleting CC-licensed CadenceUX explanations.

record_format.section_lines: Inclusive 1-based lines in the complete pinned upstream reference, not the adaptation
record_format.examples: Each tuple is [upstream_start_line, upstream_end_line, replacement_topic, test_level]. One range can contain a multi-line expression, a paired equivalent expression, or two locale illustrations embedded in the same prose line. Every secondary concrete example is mapped. Retained abstract API expressions and numeric parameter definitions are facts rather than concrete examples.
record_format.reason: Default reason applies to every example unless section-specific reason is supplied
record_format.replacement_locator: The same named function or pattern in filemaker-pro/references/<file>; overview examples appear under the corresponding arithmetic basics heading

default_reason: Independently authored domain scenario replaces concrete source expression/data while preserving the illustrated behavior and associated caveats; no original example block is recorded here.

test_levels.L: Selected deterministic expectations checked by independent Python arithmetic/calendar/text models; syntax reviewed against catalog. Not FileMaker execution, coercion, locale or renderer validation.
test_levels.S: Signature checked against catalog and example manually reviewed for the intended semantics; expected result not executed in FileMaker or independently asserted locally.
test_levels.K: Signature checked and expected kind manually reviewed only: field/Get/locale/font/format/serialization dependence prevents a fixed environment-independent result. No FileMaker or rendering execution.
test_levels.P: Explanatory prose/metadata retained or adapted, with source links and factual caveats; not an executable example.

checks: Complete upstream files read: text 495 lines; date/time 516 lines
All 64 original function headings matched to replacement function headings
All 64 signatures reviewed against factual catalog
Unicode character/code packing, text filtering/slicing/positions/lengths, replacement/insertion, numeric sorting, serial carry, whitespace and substitution-order models
Python Gregorian ordinal, named weekday, leap day, month/day overflow, clamped month shift, ISO week boundaries and generalized fiscal-week model
Weekday numbering/next-business-day arithmetic for all seven weekdays; all twelve calendar/fiscal quarters
140 half-open business-day intervals checked twice: initial full-week/remainder model against daily count, then final backward-tail expression against daily count (280 assertions, locally only)
RGB arithmetic, fractional hours, second overflow, decimal-hour conversion and H:MM duration arithmetic
limitations: Local Python models are not FileMaker engine validation; they cannot establish engine coercion, storage typing, Unicode edge behavior or full runtime validity.
No installed-font, WebDirect, styled-text serialization, field or locale-dependent output was executed.
Generalized fiscal weeks are modeled with the four-day-first-week rule; custom-start engine behavior is not established by that model.
Date/time creation-system formatting rules and legacy fontScript acceptance are retained upstream guidance, not newly tested assertions.
Business-day replacement requires end >= start and excludes public holidays; it preserves full-week arithmetic and at most six tail iterations. While requires version 18 or later.
The upstream 140 engine-tested date pairs claim is explicitly historical, distinct from this adaptation's 140 local-model interval checks.
ISO parser assumes valid input, age/anniversary examples retain Date overflow behavior, and sortable timestamp text is minute-resolution without timezone conversion.
No claim of legal clearance or endorsement is made; no other repository attribution or packaging documents were edited within this limited assignment.
